Proponents of biological sex categories argue that if complete physiological normalization is technically impossible to guarantee for a subset of the population, then the "window period" for testing must be monolithic and rigid, positing that even minor residual advantages create an unwinnable competitive environment for authentic female athletes. This side's logic holds that fairness in sport is not achieved by balancing individual metrics but by maintaining a distinct biological barrier that prevents any realistic advantage, regardless of individual hormonal recovery rates. Conversely, the counter-logic rests on the efficacy of current regulatory protocols (like strict TOL thresholds) which suggest that with consistent adherence, the performance gap can be made statistically insignificant, prioritizing the right to compete over the theoretical "perfect" uniformity of the female category.
